content.text:
This figure is from AC 43.13-2B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Alterations. Its caption: "FIGURE 11-2. PRESSURE DROP DATA FOR SMOOTH TUBING".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure is a nomograph used to determine pressure drop in smooth tubing based on air flow and tubing size/length.

Labels, values, units, part numbers, and notes printed in the figure:

- Y-axis label: PRESSURE DROP PER TEN FOOT LENGTH - INCHES OF MERCURY
- Y-axis values: 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0
- X-axis label: AIR FLOW - CUBIC FEET PER MINUTE
- X-axis values: 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20
- Diagonal line label: 1/4 * .035
- Diagonal line label: TUBING SIZE 5/16 * .035
- Diagonal line label: 3/8 * .035
- Diagonal line label: 1/2 * .042
- Diagonal line label: 5/8 * .042
- Diagonal line label: 3/4 * .049
